Ananias and Sapphira.</title> <div sID="gen30117" type="x-p"/> "The first trace of a shade upon the bright form of the young Church. Probably among the new Christians a kind of holy rivalry had sprung up, every one eager to place his means at the disposal of the apostles" [Olshausen]. Thus might the new-born zeal of some outrun their abiding principle, while others might be tempted to seek credit for a liberality which was not in their character.<div eID="gen30117" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30118" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15626"/><hi type="bold">2. kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it--</hi>The coolness with which they planned the deception aggravated the guilt of this couple.<div eID="gen30118" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30119" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">brought a certain part--</hi>pretending it to be the whole proceeds of the sale. <div eID="gen30119" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 5 Ac 5:1-11 . Ananias and Sapphira. "The first trace of a shade upon the bright form of the young Church. Probably among the new Christians a kind of holy rivalry had sprung up, every one eager to place his means at the disposal of the apostles" [Olshausen]. Thus might the new-born zeal of some outrun their abiding principle, while others might be tempted to seek credit for a liberality which was not in their character. 2. kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it-- The coolness with which they planned the deception aggravated the guilt of this couple. brought a certain part-- pretending it to be the whole proceeds of the sale.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv15648"/><div sID="gen30149" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv15648"/><hi type="bold">31. Prince and a Saviour--</hi>the first word expressing that Royalty which all Israel looked for in Messiah, the second the Saving character of it which they had utterly lost sight of. Each of these features in our Lord's work enters into the other, and both make one glorious whole (compare <reference osisRef="Acts.3.15">Ac 3:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.2.10">He 2:10</reference>).<div eID="gen30149" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30150" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to give--</hi>dispensing as a "Prince."<div eID="gen30150" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen30151" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">repentance and remission of sins--</hi>as a "Saviour"; "repentance" embracing all that change which issues in the faith which secures "forgiveness" (compare <reference osisRef="Acts.2.38">Ac 2:38</reference>; 20:21). How gloriously is Christ here exhibited; not, as in other places, as the Medium, but as the Dispenser of all spiritual blessings! <div eID="gen30151" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 31. Prince and a Saviour-- the first word expressing that Royalty which all Israel looked for in Messiah, the second the Saving character of it which they had utterly lost sight of. Each of these features in our Lord's work enters into the other, and both make one glorious whole (compare Ac 3:15 ; He 2:10 ). to give-- dispensing as a "Prince." repentance and remission of sins-- as a "Saviour"; "repentance" embracing all that change which issues in the faith which secures "forgiveness" (compare Ac 2:38 ; 20:21). How gloriously is Christ here exhibited; not, as in other places, as the Medium, but as the Dispenser of all spiritual blessings!

Then stood up ... Gamaliel--</hi>in all probability one of that name celebrated in the Jewish writings for his wisdom, the son of Simeon (possibly the same who took the infant Saviour in his arms, <reference osisRef="Luke.2.25-Luke.2.35">Lu 2:25-35</reference>), and grandson of Hillel, another celebrated rabbi. He died eighteen years before the destruction of Jerusalem [Lightfoot]. <div eID="gen30155" type="x-p"/>
